$comment: Canonical Layout_Engine metrics shared by BOTH clients (Requirement 13.1).
The Mobile_Client (Dart, flutter_app/lib/core/layout/layout_mode.dart) and
the Web_Client (TypeScript, react_app/src/core/layout.ts) each hold these
numbers as their own single authority, because a Dart file cannot import a
TypeScript file and vice versa. That duplication is a necessity, not a
choice, so the two copies can silently drift. This file is the referee: it
records the numbers once, at the repo root outside both client trees, and
each client's compliance suite reads it and asserts its own constants equal
it. A divergence in either client fails that client's suite, naming this
file as the authority both were measured against.
Read by:
- react_app/src/__tests__/compliance/metrics-examples.node.test.ts
- flutter_app/test/compliance/metrics_examples_test.dart
medium.contentMax is null, not a sentinel: Medium imposes no content cap,
and both clients model that as null (Dart double?, TS number | null). The
cross-client comparison therefore treats null === null as agreement.
This is the first fixture under test_fixtures/; task 9.1 adds more, so the
directory is a shared convention rather than a one-off. Units are CSS/
logical pixels. gutter/pad are multiples of 8 (Requirement 1.8); the 560 and
1440 content caps and the 16/24/32 metrics are the fixed WattVision values
and are allowed to appear here and in test expectations as literals.

subCompactRule.$comment: A sub-320 viewport still resolves to Compact with 16 outer padding (Requirement 2.11 totality). No floor below which resolution is undefined.
